newsitem.title: USA: Massachusetts puts moratorium on Internet sales tax.
newsitem.headline: Massachusetts puts moratorium on Internet sales tax.

text.p: Declaring Massachusetts an "Internet tax-free zone," Acting Governor Paul Cellucci Thursday declared a 16-month moratorium on collecting a 5 percent sales tax from Internet service providers.

"This is a glitch on the tax code that is threatening the continued growth of this industry," Cellucci said at the Macworld Expo trade show in Boston. "Starting today we will not collect an Internet sales tax anymore."
The moratorium will last until December next year. Cellucci called on the state legislature to pass legislation making the tax cut permanent.

Cellucci also called for the state legislature to pass the administration's telecommunications tax cut bill, which would make the Internet tax cut retroactive to 1990 and enable computer users to receive a direct rebate or the credit for the taxes they have paid to date.
The moratorium will cost the state about $1 million annually, and a retroactive payment would cost about $6 million, Cellucci said.
More than 70 Internet companies in the state have been fuelling much of the growth in the jobs in Massachusetts, Cellucci said.

"In calling for the moratorium on Internet taxation in Massachusetts, Gov. Cellucci has ensured that an industry that was born here will continue to thrive here," said Chris Anderson, vice president of the Massachusetts High Tech Council, an industry association.
The moratorium puts Massachusetts on an equal footing with other states such as Florida, California, Washington and New York, he said.
